newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chips close flat, 2nd board rebounds.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chips close flat, 2nd board rebounds.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip equities closed almost flat on Tuesday while the Second Board staged a rebound.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed down 0.26 point to 1176.81. The Second Board index which tracks small-capitalised stocks rebounded to close 10.67 points higher to 633.08.
Over 239 million shares were traded, valued at 2,067 million ringgit.
"There's really nothing to talk about; no value to add," said an institutional dealer in Singapore.
Gainers outpaced losers 368 to 177, with 163 stocks remaining unchanged.
Analysts were divided over the effects of the U.S. general election, to be held later on Tuesday, on the local bourse.
"There will always be concern over the results of the elections there, but there is no direct correlation," said Audrey Ho, head of research at Mohaiyani Securities.
"The market here is a bit cautious over the U.S. elections. If Clinton loses, and the Dow drops, there will be a reaction here," said Fiona Leong, head of research at JM Sassoon.
